enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1206 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

...New DISCUSSION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1202 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

 - A cold front has pushed through today bringing continued breezy
   and windy conditions with well below normal temperatures.

 - High wind warning and wind advisory still in effect through
   tonight for southwest New Mexico. Wind gusts to 50 mph are 
   possible in New Mexico bootheel.
   

 - Scattered rain showers for the middle of next week as 
   temperatures rebound. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1202 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Today, we will see our coldest temperatures of the season so far 
with lows dipping down to the low 40s through much of the lowlands. 
Area mountains will see subfreezing conditions with the Sacs 
reaching the low 20s in some parts during tomorrow's early morning. 
These temperature trends are about 15 to 20 degrees below normal for 
this time of year. High temperatures will rebound by the end of the 
weekend. Widespread sustained easterly winds between 20 and 30 mph 
will continue this afternoon and evening with gusts exceeding 50 mph 
at times in parts of southern Hidalgo county.

Blowing dust remains a concern through this evening coinciding with 
the greatest wind threat in southern Hidalgo county according to the 
signatures in the RRFS. A Blowing Dust Advisory near the Lordsburg 
Playa, NM Bootheel, and Luna county is in effect through 8 PM 
tonight.

Winds subside and precip chances are rather slim for most of the 
weekend with greater chances favoring the western half of the CWA on 
Sunday morning as a developing upper level low pushes east. This low 
deepens considerably over the course of next week bringing with it 
increasing chances for precip. Flooding is possible with areawide 
rain and PWs reaching around 1 inch. Confidence remains low for 
midweek rain impacts at this time.

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1152 AM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Breezy to windy conditions will start to slowly decrease tonight. 
Winds out in western NM (like KDMN) and the higher terrain stays 
quite breezy tonight. Saturday will become breezy as well but not to 
the level that we saw last night or today. Breezier winds out in 
KDMN tomorrow afternoon and continued dry conditions.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 548 AM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

A cold front ushered in strong winds and some blowing dust this
morning. These elevated winds will continue through most of the 
day, before slowing this evening. Min RH's today and Saturday will
be in the mid to upper teens in the lowlands and in the 20's in 
area mountains. Sunday will start both a warming trend and 
moisture will return to the region. Rain chances will be back in 
the forecast for much of next week, with min RH's above 30% across
the area. Ventilation rates today will be very good to excellent 
and then a little lower on Saturday.

&&
